title: Georgia Red Clay Crawlspace Moisture & Subfloor Fungal Decay
gbp:

Metro Atlanta’s heavy clay soil acts like an underground sponge, trapping thousands of gallons of hydrostatic groundwater right against foundation footings.

• Relative humidity above 70%—the exact threshold for wood-destroying fungus and mold.
• Block foundation step-cracking from expansive clay soils.
• Subterranean termite mud tubes bridging into subfloors.

Residential heating system evaluation is one of the most critical life-safety checkpoints in Georgia property due diligence. Gas-fired forced-air furnaces rely on a sealed heat exchanger to isolate combustion byproducts (including Carbon Monoxide, Nitrous Oxides, and unburned hydrocarbons) from the conditioned supply air stream.

Corrosion, persistent flame impingement, or reduced airflow across the evaporator coil lead to metal fatigue and cell breach. When a heat exchanger crack develops, the blower fan pressurizes the combustion chamber, creating flame rollout and venting CO directly into living quarters.
